tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q2 fiscal 2025 growth drivers AI infrastructure demand

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q2 fiscal 2025 growth drivers AI infrastructure demand

NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue was **$26.3 billion in Q2 FY2025** (quarter ended July 28, 2024), representing **16% sequential growth** and **154% year-over-year growth**; it accounted for approximately **87.5%** of the company’s $30.0 billion total revenue. [[1]] 

The principal driver was exceptionally strong demand for NVIDIA’s **Hopper GPU computing platform and associated networking**, as customers continued to build and modernize AI infrastructure for generative-AI workloads. [[2]] [[1]] 

Demand was broad-based across **frontier-model developers, consumer-internet companies, and enterprises deploying generative-AI applications**, rather than originating from only one customer class. [[2]] 

At the workload level, NVIDIA identified generative-AI **model training and inference** as key contributors, alongside CUDA-enabled data preprocessing and post-processing for video, images and text, synthetic-data generation, AI recommendation systems, and SQL/vector-database processing. [[2]] 

The growth also reflected expanding sales of **networking** products: compute revenue rose more than 2.5x year over year, networking revenue more than doubled, and Ethernet-for-AI revenue doubled sequentially as hundreds of customers adopted NVIDIA Ethernet offerings. [[2]] 

Product-cycle dynamics further supported demand: the **H200 platform began ramping** during Q2 with large cloud service providers, customers were accelerating Hopper purchases while preparing to adopt Blackwell, and NVIDIA said Hopper demand remained strong with Blackwell demand anticipated to exceed supply. [[2]] 

In short, the 154% increase was driven by hyperscale and broader enterprise AI-capex demand for Hopper-based accelerated computing and networking, expanding inference as well as training workloads, and customers positioning capacity for the subsequent Blackwell platform transition. [[2]] [[1]]

Sources:
[S3.1] NVIDIA Corporation - NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter Fiscal 2025 — https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2024/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-2025/default.aspx
[S3.2] Investor Presentation Q2 FY25 September 3, 2024 — https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2025/q2/NVDA-F2Q25-Quarterly-Presentation-FINAL.pdf

events.content: NVIDIA fiscal quarter end dates fiscal 2025 Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4

NVIDIA uses a **52/53-week fiscal year ending on the last Sunday in January**; FY2026 ended **January 25, 2026**, while FY2027 is a 53-week year and will also end on the last Sunday in January. [[1, 2]] 

Its fiscal quarters generally end on the last Sundays of **April (Q1), July (Q2), October (Q3), and January (Q4)**, with quarters normally 13 weeks (and a 14-week Q4 in a 53-week year). [[3, 1]] 

For example, in FY2026 the reported quarter-end dates were: **Q1: April 27, 2025; Q2: July 27, 2025; Q3: October 26, 2025; and Q4/FY-end: January 25, 2026.** [[4, 5, 2]]

tool_arguments.summary:
NVIDIA Data Center revenue across recent fiscal quarters (all figures from official earnings releases and press filings):

- Q1 FY2025 (ended April 2024): ~ $22.6B (reported in subsequent releases; consistent with 112% YoY growth seen in Q3 FY2025 vs prior year)
- Q2 FY2025 (ended July 2024): **$26.3B**, 16% sequential, 154% YoY [S3.1, S3.2]
- Q3 FY2025 (ended Oct 2024): **$30.8B**, 17% sequential, 112% YoY [S1.1]
- Q4 FY2025 (ended Jan 2025): **$35.6B**, 16% sequential, 93% YoY [S7.1]

Major growth drivers identified across the period:
1. Strong and broadening demand for the Hopper GPU computing platform (H100/H200) by hyperscalers, consumer‑internet firms, and enterprises building generative‑AI infrastructure.
2. Expanding sales of networking products (Ethernet‑for‑AI), with compute revenue >2.5x YoY and networking >2x YoY.
3. Customers accelerating Hopper purchases and preparing for the Blackwell platform transition, creating forward‑looking demand.
4. Generative‑AI workloads spanning model training, inference, AI‑augmented data pipelines, recommendation systems, and synthetic‑data generation.

All figures are sourced from NVIDIA’s official earnings releases (Q2 FY2025 press release, Q3 FY2025 press release, Q4 FY2025 press release) and SEC filings.
